whyEn: This chapter is the reference library the exam quietly assumes you own: age-banded vital signs (a newborn pulse of 140 is healthy; the same number in a grandfather is an emergency), the weight and milestone arithmetic of the first year, and the stage names — toddler, preschooler, school-age, adolescent, early/middle/late adult — that anchor questions across pediatrics, geriatrics, and communication. It also plants two clinical time bombs the written exam loves: the infant airway that occludes at the slightest excuse, and the shrunken older brain that bleeds silently into its own empty space after minor head trauma. Weight is low as a standalone chapter, but its numbers resurface inside almost every scenario stem that names an age. Learn the tables cold; the psychosocial stages need only one clean pass.
whyZh: 这一章是考试默认你随身携带的『参考手册』：按年龄分段的生命体征（新生儿脉搏140是健康，同一个数字出现在爷爷身上就是急症）、第一年的体重与里程碑算术，以及幼儿、学龄前、学龄、青少年、成年早中晚期这些锚定术语——儿科、老年、沟通各章的题干全靠它们定位。它还埋了笔试最爱引爆的两颗临床炸弹：动辄堵死的婴儿气道，和轻微头外伤后往萎缩空腔里悄悄出血的老年大脑。作为独立章节权重不高，但只要题干里出现年龄，这章的数字就会回来找你。数值表要背到条件反射；心理社会阶段过一遍干净的即可。

sections.titleEn: Infants (1 Month to 1 Year): The Fastest-Changing Patient You Will Meet
sections.titleZh: 婴儿期（1个月～1岁）：变化最快的患者

points.en: Age labels are testable on their own: a neonate is birth to 1 month (covered in the neonatology chapter), and an infant is 1 month to 1 year. The rule across childhood: the younger the person, the faster the pulse and respirations.
points.zh: 年龄标签本身就是考点：新生儿指出生到1个月（详见新生儿章），婴儿指1个月到1岁。整个儿童期的总规律：年龄越小，脉搏和呼吸越快。

points.en: Printed vitals at birth: average pulse 140 beats/min, respirations 30 to 60 breaths/min, oxygen saturation normal at 94% or greater. Blood glucose is normally at least 2.5 mmol/L at birth, rising to at least 3.3 mmol/L from age 1 month onward (the book prints 45 and 60 mg/dL).
points.zh: 出生时的印刷基准值：平均脉搏140次/分，呼吸30～60次/分，血氧饱和度正常应≥94%。血糖出生时正常≥2.5 mmol/L，满1个月起升至≥3.3 mmol/L（书中印刷为 45/60 mg/dL）。

points.en: Tidal volume starts at 6 to 8 mL/kg in the newborn and grows to 10 to 15 mL/kg by age 1 year.
points.zh: 潮气量：新生儿期为6～8 mL/kg，到1岁增至10～15 mL/kg。

points.en: In children, blood pressure tracks body weight, so it climbs with age: average systolic pressure is 67 to 84 mm Hg at birth and reaches 85 to 104 mm Hg by age 1 year.
points.zh: 儿童的血压与体重直接对应，随年龄上升：出生时平均收缩压67～84 mmHg，1岁时达到85～104 mmHg。

points.en: Weight curve of the first year: a full-term newborn weighs about 3.4 kg; in week one it sheds 5% to 10% of birth weight as fluid loss, regains from the second week, then grows roughly 30 g per day — doubling birth weight by 6 months and tripling it by 1 year.
points.zh: 第一年的体重曲线：足月新生儿约3.4 kg；出生第一周因体液丢失掉5%～10%的出生体重，第二周起回升，此后以每天约30 g的速度增长——6个月体重翻倍，1岁达到出生时的三倍。

points.en: Infants breathe mainly through the nose for their first several months, and babies under 6 months are especially prone to nasal congestion from viral upper respiratory infections — so on any 'choking infant' call, confirm first that the nasal passages are not blocked by mucus.
points.zh: 婴儿出生后头几个月主要靠鼻呼吸，6个月以下尤其容易因病毒性上呼吸道感染而鼻塞——所以凡是『婴儿呛噎』的呼叫，第一步先确认鼻道有没有被黏液堵住。

points.en: Infant chest mechanics: the rib cage is softer than an adult's, ribs lie horizontally, intercostal and accessory muscles are underdeveloped, and the diaphragm is the main breathing muscle. Practical consequences — the abdomen bulges with each breath while the chest barely moves (count respirations at the abdomen), and the infant fatigues fast when breathing gets hard.
points.zh: 婴儿的胸廓力学：肋弓比成人软，肋骨呈水平走向，肋间肌和辅助呼吸肌都未发育好，膈肌是主要的呼吸肌。落到实操上——每次吸气看到的是腹部鼓起而胸廓几乎不动（数呼吸要看腹部起伏），而且一旦呼吸费力，婴儿很快就会疲劳。

points.en: Two airway facts that drive equipment choice: an infant's tongue is proportionally larger inside the mouth, and the airway is proportionally shorter and narrower — so the infant airway occludes far more easily than an older child's or adult's, and adjunct and endotracheal tube sizing must respect that anatomy.
points.zh: 决定器材选择的两条气道事实：婴儿的舌头相对口腔偏大，气道相对更短更窄——因此婴儿气道远比大孩子和成人容易被堵住，选口咽通气道和气管导管尺寸时必须迁就这套解剖。

points.en: Infants have a smaller functional residual capacity, fewer alveoli, and burn oxygen faster — an apneic infant slides into respiratory failure sooner than a child or adult, so watch closely.
points.zh: 婴儿的功能残气量更小、肺泡更少、耗氧更快——出现呼吸暂停的婴儿比儿童和成人更快滑向呼吸衰竭，必须紧盯。

points.en: Renal immaturity: newborn kidneys concentrate urine and excrete water poorly, so infants dehydrate easily and cannot compensate the way adults do; their urine is mostly water, which also sets them up for electrolyte imbalances.
points.zh: 肾脏不成熟：新生儿的肾浓缩尿液和排水的能力都差，所以婴儿极易脱水、且无法像成人那样代偿；他们的尿液以水为主，这又埋下了电解质紊乱的隐患。

points.en: First-year immunity is borrowed: antibodies collected from maternal blood in the womb give naturally acquired passive immunity that persists through much of the first year, topped up by antibodies delivered in breast milk.
points.zh: 第一年的免疫力是『借来的』：胎儿期从母血获得的抗体构成天然获得性被动免疫，可维持出生后第一年的大部分时间，母乳中的抗体再为其加码。

points.en: Four newborn reflexes to match on sight: Moro (startle) — arms fly wide, fingers spread, grabbing motion when caught off guard; palmar grasp — fingers close around an object placed in the palm; rooting — head turns toward a touch on the cheek; sucking — triggered by stroking the lips. Cranial-nerve functions (blinking, sucking, gag) are the most developed motor-sensory pathways at birth.
points.zh: 四个必须一眼配对的新生儿反射：Moro（惊跳）反射——受惊时双臂张开、五指展开、做抓握状；掌握反射——物体放进手心即五指合拢；觅食反射——脸颊被碰即转头寻找；吸吮反射——轻触嘴唇即触发。出生时发育最完善的运动感觉通路在脑神经（眨眼、吸吮、咽反射）。

points.en: Fontanelles let the skull bones mould during birth-canal passage; the skull plates fuse into suture joints by age 2 years. Assessment payoff: a sunken anterior fontanelle can be a sign of dehydration.
points.zh: 囟门让颅骨在通过产道时得以变形；颅骨各骨片到2岁前后融合成骨缝。评估价值：前囟凹陷可能是脱水的征象。

points.en: Sleep milestone parents will quote to you: most infants can sleep 5 hours at a stretch by age 3 months, though some take until 1 year.
points.zh: 家长最常挂在嘴边的睡眠里程碑：多数婴儿3个月大就能连睡5小时，也有的要到1岁才做到。

points.en: Musculoskeletal numbers: longitudinal bone growth happens at the growth (epiphyseal) plates on each end of the long bones, bones thicken by building on themselves, and muscle makes up roughly 25% of an infant's total weight.
points.zh: 肌骨系统的数字：长骨的纵向生长发生在两端的生长板（骺板），骨骼靠自我叠加而增粗，肌肉约占婴儿总体重的25%。

points.en: Milestones, months 2 to 6: at 2 months recognizes familiar faces and tracks objects with the eyes; 3 months brings objects to the mouth, smiles and frowns; 4 months reaches out to people and drools; 5 months sleeps through the night and tells family from strangers; 6 months starts teething, sits upright in a chair, says one-syllable words.
points.zh: 2～6个月的里程碑：2个月认得熟悉的脸、眼睛会追物；3个月把东西往嘴里送、会笑会皱眉；4个月伸手要人抱、流口水；5个月能睡整夜、分得清家人和陌生人；6个月开始出牙、能坐在椅子上、会说单音节词。

points.en: Milestones, months 7 to 12: at 7 months fears strangers and has mood swings; 8 months responds to 'no', sits upright, plays peek-a-boo; 9 months pulls to standing and explores objects with the mouth; 10 months responds to their own name and crawls efficiently; 11 months begins walking unaided and hates restriction; 12 months knows their name and can walk.
points.zh: 7～12个月的里程碑：7个月怕生、情绪起伏大；8个月听得懂『不行』、能坐稳、会玩躲猫猫；9个月能扶物站起、用嘴探索物品；10个月听到名字有反应、爬得利索；11个月开始不扶东西走路、讨厌被限制；12个月知道自己的名字、会走路。

points.en: Crying is the infant's primary distress channel, and parents genuinely discriminate the tones — anger, frustration, pain, fear, hunger, discomfort, sleepiness. A distinct alarming distressed cry signals a situational crisis triggered by an unexpected event; treat the parent's 'this cry is different' as data.
points.zh: 哭是婴儿表达痛苦的主渠道，家长真能听出哭声的分别——生气、受挫、疼痛、害怕、饿了、不舒服、困了。若出现一种异样的惊恐哭声，提示突发事件引起的情境危机；家长那句『这次哭得不一样』要当作有效信息。

points.en: Attachment vocabulary: bonding is a close personal relationship built on secure attachment — the infant has learned that caregivers respond to needs, which frees them to explore. Anxious avoidant attachment appears in repeatedly rejected infants, who build an isolated style that depends on nobody. Trust versus mistrust is the developmental stage from birth to about 18 months: a planned, organized, routine world earns the caregivers the infant's trust — and its absence earns the opposite.
points.zh: 依恋的术语题：亲密纽带（bonding）建立在安全型依恋之上——婴儿确信照护者会回应需求，才敢放心探索。反复遭拒绝的婴儿则形成焦虑回避型依恋，活成谁也不依赖的孤立样式。信任对不信任是出生到约18个月的发展阶段：有计划、有条理、有规律的世界让婴儿信任照护者——反之则收获不信任。

sections.titleEn: Toddlers (1–2) and Preschoolers (3–5): Immunity on Its Own, Words on the Way
sections.titleZh: 幼儿期（1～2岁）与学龄前期（3～5岁）：免疫自立，语言起步

points.en: Definitions and vitals trend: toddlers are 1 to 2 years old, preschoolers 3 to 5. Compared with infants, their pulse and respiratory rates slow down while systolic blood pressure rises to roughly 100 mm Hg — and the steep weight gain of infancy levels off.
points.zh: 定义与生命体征走向：幼儿指1～2岁，学龄前儿童指3～5岁。与婴儿相比，脉搏和呼吸都变慢，收缩压升到约100 mmHg——婴儿期陡峭的体重增长曲线在此放平。

points.en: The toddler cardiovascular system already works much like an adult's, and the lungs keep adding bronchioles and alveoli — but lung musculature stays underdeveloped, so toddlers and preschoolers cannot sustain deep or rapid breathing for long.
points.zh: 幼儿的心血管系统已与成人相差不大，肺还在继续增生细支气管和肺泡——但呼吸肌发育跟不上，所以幼儿和学龄前儿童没法长时间维持深呼吸或快呼吸。

points.en: The signature immune event of this stage is losing the mother's passive immunity: frequent common colds appear, showing up as gastrointestinal distress or upper respiratory infections, while time spent with playmates and classmates exposes the child to viruses and germs and builds an immunity of their own.
points.zh: 这个阶段最标志性的免疫事件是母传被动免疫的消失：孩子开始频繁『中招』，普通感冒常表现为胃肠不适或上呼吸道感染；而与玩伴、同学厮混的过程恰恰让身体接触各种病毒细菌，攒出属于自己的免疫力。

points.en: Neuromuscular growth surges as the child field-tests the nervous system — walking, running, jumping, playing catch; the renal system matures in parallel and elimination patterns come under control, which is what toilet training rides on.
points.zh: 神经肌肉发育突飞猛进，孩子用走、跑、跳、抛接球把整套神经系统实测了一遍；肾脏系统同步成熟，排泄规律逐渐可控——如厕训练正是踩着这个生理基础进行的。

points.en: Baby teeth erupt during this window; teething — teeth breaking through the gums — can hurt and can be accompanied by fever. Do not let 'he's just teething' end an assessment, but know the textbook links the two.
points.zh: 乳牙在这个窗口萌出；出牙（牙齿顶破牙龈）可以很疼，还可能伴随发热。别让一句『他在出牙』终结你的评估，但要知道教材确实把两者挂了钩。

points.en: Language milestone: by age 3 or 4 most children use and understand full sentences, progressing from language as a tool to get what they want toward creative, playful use of words.
points.zh: 语言里程碑：3～4岁时多数孩子已能说出并听懂完整句子，语言的用途也从『要东西的工具』升级为带创造性、游戏性的表达。

points.en: Play is the psychosocial curriculum: games teach self-control, rule-following, and competitiveness; much learning happens by watching peers on group outings — and by watching television and the Internet, which is why some parents ration screen content and time. Children in this stage also learn to recognize sexual differences by observing role models.
points.zh: 游戏就是这个阶段的心理社会课程：玩游戏教会自控、守规则和竞争意识；集体活动里看同伴怎么做，本身就是学习——看电视和上网同样是学习渠道，所以有的家长要限制内容和时长。这个阶段的孩子还会通过观察身边的榜样人物识别性别差异。

sections.titleEn: School-Age Children (6–12): Growth in Centimetres, Reasoning in Stages
sections.titleZh: 学龄期（6～12岁）：身体按厘米长，思维按阶段升

points.en: From 6 to 12 years, vital signs and body proportions drift steadily toward adult values; the child gains about 2.5 to 3.5 kg and 5 to 6 cm per year, and the permanent teeth come in during this period.
points.zh: 6～12岁间，生命体征和身体比例都在稳步逼近成人水平；孩子每年增重约2.5～3.5 kg、长高5～6 cm，恒牙也在这个阶段替换乳牙。

points.en: Three reasoning stages to keep straight for the exam: preconventional — the child acts to avoid punishment and to get what they want; conventional — the child seeks approval from peers and society; postconventional — decisions are guided by the child's own conscience.
points.zh: 考试要分清的三种推理阶段：前习俗推理——行为几乎只为躲避惩罚、得到想要的东西；习俗推理——行为为了赢得同伴和社会的认可；后习俗推理——由自己的良知来指挥决定。

points.en: Two self-terms that examiners like to swap: self-concept is how we perceive ourselves; self-esteem is how we feel about ourselves and how we fit in with peers. Both take shape in the school years — a phase when parents, as a whole, spend less time with their children.
points.zh: 出题人爱互换的两个『自我』：自我概念是我们对自己的认知；自尊是我们对自己的感受、以及和同伴『合不合群』的体验。两者都在学龄期成形——而这恰是家长整体上陪伴变少的阶段。

sections.titleZh: 青少年期（13～18岁）：体征成人化，心理动荡期

points.en: Adolescent (13 to 18 years) vitals settle into adult ranges: systolic blood pressure generally 110 to 131 mm Hg, pulse 60 to 100 beats/min, respirations 12 to 20 breaths/min.
points.zh: 青少年（13～18岁）的生命体征落入成人区间：收缩压一般110～131 mmHg，脉搏60～100次/分，呼吸12～20次/分。

points.en: The growth spurt — a surge of muscle and bone growth plus blood changes — hits girls earlier than boys, but once growth finishes, boys generally end up taller and physically stronger.
points.zh: 青春期猛长（肌肉与骨骼的快速生长外加血液成分变化）在女孩身上来得比男孩早，但长完之后，男孩通常更高、力气更大。

points.en: Secondary sexual development: external sex organs enlarge, pubic and axillary hair appear, the voice changes in range and depth; in girls, adipose deposits enlarge breasts and thighs, and menstruation begins — with menarche arriving at ever-younger ages, first bleeding before the teen years is not uncommon.
points.zh: 第二性征发育：外生殖器增大，阴毛和腋毛出现，嗓音的音域和音色改变；女孩的乳房和大腿因脂肪沉积而丰满，月经来潮——而且初潮年龄越来越提前，不到十三岁就来月经并不罕见。

points.en: Hormone axis, girls versus boys: in girls, follicle-stimulating hormone and luteinizing hormone are released and drive up estrogen and progesterone; in boys, gonadotropin secretion leads to testosterone production. The hormonal turmoil is also why acne appears.
points.zh: 激素轴的男女对照：女孩释放促卵泡激素（FSH）和黄体生成素（LH），推高雌激素和孕酮；男孩分泌促性腺激素，产出睾酮。痤疮正是这场激素风暴的副产品。

points.en: Psychosocial profile: family conflict over control of the teenager's life, privacy battles with parents and siblings, an identity still under construction, growing interest in sexual relations, fixation on public image with terror of embarrassment, and a personal code of ethics assembled partly from parents' values and partly from the surrounding environment.
points.zh: 心理社会画像：为『谁说了算』与家人冲突不断，同父母和兄弟姐妹争夺隐私，身份认同还在搭建中，对性关系的兴趣上升，极度在意公众形象、最怕当众出丑，个人伦理准则一半继承自父母的价值观、一半来自周遭环境。

points.en: The exam-critical risk fact: adolescents carry a higher risk of suicide and depression than other populations — a screening thought that belongs in every teenage patient contact.
points.zh: 必考的风险事实：青少年的自杀与抑郁风险高于其他人群——接触任何一名少年患者时，这根筛查的弦都要绷着。

sections.titleEn: Early Adults (19–40): Peak, Then the First Slow Decline
sections.titleZh: 成年早期（19～40岁）：巅峰，以及第一道下坡

points.en: Early adulthood spans 19 to 40 years. Ideal vitals: pulse around 70 beats/min, respirations 12 to 20 breaths/min, blood pressure about 120/80 mm Hg.
points.zh: 成年早期指19～40岁。理想生命体征：脉搏约70次/分，呼吸12～20次/分，血压约120/80 mmHg。

points.en: The body peaks from 19 to just past 25. Between 25 and 30, intervertebral disks begin to settle — height can measurably 'shrink' — while fatty tissue increases and brings weight gain, muscle strength declines, and reflexes slow.
points.zh: 身体机能的巅峰从19岁维持到刚过25岁。25～30岁之间，椎间盘开始沉降——身高会出现可测的『缩水』——同时脂肪组织增加带来体重上升，肌力下降，反射变慢。

points.en: Sarcopenia by the numbers: muscle-mass loss starts at middle age at roughly 1% per year and in severe cases reaches about 50% loss by the eighties or nineties. Physical activity started at any age can partly minimize or even reverse it; in its advanced stage it becomes a component of the late-life frailty syndrome.
points.zh: 肌少症的数字：肌肉量从中年起以每年约1%的速度流失，严重者到八九十岁时可丢掉约50%。任何年龄开始规律运动都能部分延缓甚至逆转；进展到晚期，它就成为老年衰弱综合征的组成部分。

points.en: Psychosocially the era is summed up in three words — work, family, stress: adults fight to carve out their place, settle down, pair off, and have children. Paradoxically, despite the load, this remains one of the more stable periods of life.
points.zh: 心理社会层面可用三个词概括——工作、家庭、压力：人在这个阶段拼命给自己在世界上挣一个位置，安家、恋爱、生子。吊诡的是，尽管负重前行，这仍是人生中相对稳定的时期之一。

sections.titleEn: Middle Adults (41–60): Health Diverges, Goals Sharpen
sections.titleZh: 成年中期（41～60岁）：健康开始分化，目标开始聚焦

points.en: Middle adulthood runs 41 to 60 years. The body's weak spots of the era: vision and hearing loss, rising cardiovascular problems, and a greater incidence of cancer. In women, menopause — the cessation of menstruation — begins in the late 40s or early 50s.
points.zh: 成年中期指41～60岁。这一时期的身体软肋：视力和听力下降、心血管问题增多、癌症发生率上升。女性的绝经（月经终止）始于40多岁末到50岁出头。

points.en: Assessment stance for this group: general health varies enormously with lifestyle, living environment, and each person's capacity to respond to adversity — so a middle adult is assessed as a unique case, never read off their age.
points.zh: 对这一人群的评估立场：健康状况因生活方式、居住环境和应对逆境的能力而天差地别——所以成年中期的患者必须当作独立个案来评估，绝不能按年龄想当然。

points.en: Psychosocial markers: focus turns to achieving life goals as the halfway point of life expectancy comes into view; empty nest syndrome forces a readjustment when children leave home. Newer patterns are reshaping the stage — later childbearing after early workforce entry, more people staying single (especially in urban cities), fewer marriages, nonmarital partnerships — and depending on earlier social investment, the result is more isolation for some and deeper community engagement for others.
points.zh: 心理社会标志：意识到人生过半，注意力转向完成人生目标；子女离家带来的空巢综合征迫使父母重新安排生活。新的生活模式正在改写这个阶段——早早进入职场、推迟生育，更多人保持单身（尤其在大城市），结婚的人变少、非婚伴侣关系增多——早年的社会投入不同，有人因此更孤独，有人则把精力转投社区和新的关系。

points.en: The era's worry list — living with a chronic illness or a new cancer diagnosis, plus money: consumption, debts, and retirement age are all rising. The chapter's framing: middle adults tend to treat these as challenges to overcome rather than threats to avoid.
points.zh: 这一阶段的心事清单——带着慢性病生活或刚确诊癌症，再加上钱的问题：消费、负债和退休年龄都在上涨。教材的定调是：成年中期的人倾向把这些当作要闯的关，而不是要躲的坑。

sections.titleEn: Late Adults (61+): Every System Ages on Schedule
sections.titleZh: 成年晚期（61岁以上）：每个系统都在按表衰老

points.en: Late adulthood starts at 61. Life-expectancy figures printed in the chapter: about 73 years in 1979, approximately 78 years now, with maximum life expectancy estimated at 115 years. Vitals in this group depend on overall health, medical conditions, and medications — and staying active often requires multiple medications.
points.zh: 成年晚期从61岁算起。本章印刷的预期寿命数据：1979年约73岁，如今约78岁，人类寿命上限估计为115岁。这一人群的生命体征取决于整体健康、基础疾病和用药情况——而『保持活跃』的代价常常是同时吃着多种药。

points.en: Atherosclerosis is the engine of cardiac aging: cholesterol and calcium build up inside vessel walls as plaque, most often in the coronary vessels, until flow is partly or completely blocked. The same disease weakens and bulges vessel walls into aneurysms that can rupture under stretching forces — and many people over 65 carry atherosclerotic disease.
points.zh: 动脉粥样硬化是心脏衰老的发动机：胆固醇和钙沉积在血管壁内形成斑块，最常侵犯冠状血管，直到血流被部分或完全堵死。同一种病变还会让血管壁薄弱膨出成动脉瘤，在高牵张力下可能破裂——65岁以上人群中患动脉粥样硬化的相当普遍。

points.en: The aging heart in one causal chain: heart rate falls, cardiac output drops, and the heart loses the ability to raise output on demand; systolic pressure climbs as vessels stiffen, so the left ventricle works harder, thickens, and loses elasticity — which hinders filling and cuts output further. Stiffened valves can produce a murmur even without disease, and with elastin and collagen declining, peripheral vessel elasticity falls by as much as 70%, crippling blood-pressure compensation.
points.zh: 老化心脏的因果链一口气记完：心率下降、心输出量减少、且再也无法按需求加大输出；血管变硬使收缩压升高，左心室被迫加班而增厚、失去弹性——充盈受阻，输出量进一步下滑。瓣膜僵硬后即使无病也可能听到杂音；随着弹性蛋白和胶原减少，外周血管弹性最多可降70%，血压代偿能力随之瘫痪。

points.en: Respiratory mechanics reverse the infant pattern: airway size increases while alveolar surface area shrinks, lung elasticity fades so late adults lean on their intercostal muscles, and calcification of the ribs to the sternum stiffens the chest — all of it making breathing harder work.
points.zh: 呼吸力学正好把婴儿的模式反过来：气道口径变大而肺泡表面积缩水，肺的天然弹性消退、老人只好更多动用肋间肌，肋骨与胸骨间的钙化又把胸廓变硬——每一条都在给呼吸加码。

points.en: Upper-airway defences crumble with age: secretion clearance, cough and gag reflexes all weaken, the cilia lining the airways diminish, and airway innervation feels less — so aspiration and obstruction both become more likely.
points.zh: 上气道的防线随年龄崩塌：清除分泌物的能力、咳嗽反射和咽反射一起减弱，气道内衬的纤毛减少，气道神经的感觉越来越迟钝——误吸和梗阻的概率双双上升。

points.en: Weakened lower-airway smooth muscle lets a strong inhalation collapse the airway walls inward — producing inspiratory wheezing, low flow rates through the narrowed passages, and air trapping because expiration never quite empties the alveoli.
points.zh: 下气道平滑肌无力后，用力吸气反而会把气道壁吸塌——于是出现吸气相喘鸣，变窄的通道压低气流量，呼气排不净肺泡里的气，形成气体潴留。

points.en: Volumes move in opposite directions: vital capacity drops markedly from young adulthood (respiratory muscle loss, stiffer thoracic cage, less exchange surface) while residual volume rises — stagnant air sits in the alveoli, gas exchange suffers, and the result can be hypercarbia and acidosis even at rest.
points.zh: 肺容积一降一升：肺活量较青年期显著下降（呼吸肌流失、胸廓变僵、交换面积减少），残气量却在增加——陈腐气体滞留肺泡、气体交换受阻，后果是静息状态下也可能出现高碳酸血症和酸中毒。

points.en: Kidney aging has printed spans: filtration function declines significantly between ages 20 and 90, kidney mass shrinks over the same period, and nephron numbers fall between 30 and 80 — leaving aged kidneys slow to answer hemodynamic stress and fluid-electrolyte imbalances.
points.zh: 肾脏衰老有印刷明确的时间跨度：滤过功能在20～90岁间显著下滑，肾脏质量同期缩小，肾单位数量在30～80岁间减少——老化的肾对血流动力学应激和水电解质紊乱的反应都慢了半拍。

points.en: The digestive cascade of aging: taste buds dull to salty and sweet, saliva secretion falls (weakening complex-carbohydrate processing), gastric motility slows as intestinal-tract neurons are lost — so older adults feel constipated or not hungry — and gastric acid secretion drops. Mesenteric blood flow can fall by as much as 50%, cutting nutrient extraction; gallstones grow more common, and anal sphincter changes can produce fecal incontinence.
points.zh: 消化系统的衰老连锁：味蕾对咸和甜变钝，唾液分泌减少（复杂碳水的初步消化跟着变差），肠道神经元流失使胃肠蠕动放慢——老人于是便秘、没胃口——胃酸分泌也在下降。肠系膜血流最多可掉50%，营养吸收随之缩水；胆结石越来越常见，肛门括约肌弹性改变还可能带来大便失禁。

points.en: Central nervous system by the numbers: brain weight may shrink 10% to 20% by age 80; a selective 5% to 50% of neurons are lost and the survivors shrink; the frontal lobe may lose up to 20% of its synapses across a lifetime; motor and sensory networks slow. Yet the brain's metabolic rate does not change and oxygen consumption stays constant for life.
points.zh: 中枢神经系统的数字：到80岁脑重可缩水10%～20%；神经元选择性丢失5%～50%，幸存者也在萎缩；额叶一生中最多可失去20%的突触；运动与感觉网络全面变慢。但脑的代谢率并不改变，耗氧量终生恒定。

points.en: The geriatric subdural trap: brain shrinkage opens a void between brain and outer meninges and stretches the bridging veins; trauma that jolts the brain tears these veins, blood drains into the void, and a subdural hematoma can go unnoticed — because signs of head trauma need raised intracranial pressure, and pressure will not rise until that void has filled and pressurized.
points.zh: 老年硬膜下血肿的陷阱：脑萎缩在脑与脑膜最外层之间腾出一个空腔，同时把桥静脉拉紧；外伤使脑组织晃动就能撕裂这些静脉，血正好灌进空腔——于是硬膜下血肿可以长时间毫无动静，因为颅脑外伤的体征要靠颅内压升高来表现，而空腔没被填满加压之前，颅内压根本不会升。

points.en: Peripheral nerves slow too: sensation is diminished and misread, sluggish reflexes feed the trauma rate, and deteriorating nerve endings blunt the skin's warning system — hot, cold, sharp, and wet hazards injure because the body senses them too late.
points.zh: 周围神经同样在减速：感觉减退且容易误判，反射迟钝助推外伤发生率，神经末梢退化钝化了皮肤的报警系统——烫的、冰的、尖的、湿的东西之所以伤人，是因为身体察觉得太迟。

points.en: Aging eyes: pupils run smaller and react sluggishly to light, lens opacity degrades acuity, a thickening lens struggles to focus up close, peripheral fields narrow, and glare sensitivity constricts the visual field further.
points.zh: 眼睛的衰老：瞳孔偏小、对光反应迟钝，晶状体混浊拉低视敏度，晶状体增厚使近距离聚焦吃力，周边视野收窄，对眩光的敏感又把视野压得更小。

points.en: Hearing loss is about four times more common than vision loss in late adults, typically hitting high-frequency hearing first and sometimes ending in deafness.
points.zh: 在成年晚期，听力丧失比视力丧失常见约四倍，通常先丢高频听力，部分人最终失聪。

points.en: The terminal drop hypothesis: most late adults keep high brain function until about 5 years before death, after which mental function is presumed to decline. Treat the older patient as a thinking adult — the wisdom is intact far longer than stereotypes allow.
points.zh: 终末下降假说：多数老年人直到死亡前约5年仍保有较高的脑功能，最后5年心智功能才被推定走低。所以要把老年患者当作头脑清楚的成年人对待——他们的智慧保存得远比刻板印象来得久。

points.en: Living arrangements shape the call: many refuse to give up the independence of their own home while assisted-living communities multiply — campus living with age peers, a private apartment, and optional nursing, maintenance, and meals; some are even sited next to preschools so residents can interact with children. The stay-or-move decision is limited by frailty and economics, and both length and quality of life hang on meaningful social interaction, mobility, and maximal safe independence.
points.zh: 居住方式决定出勤场景：许多老人不肯放弃自家住宅的独立性，辅助生活社区却在不断增多——与同龄人同住园区、保有私人公寓，护理、维修、餐食按需提供；有的社区甚至建在幼儿园旁边，让老人有机会与孩子互动。留家还是搬迁，受限于衰弱程度和经济状况；而寿命与生活质量，都系于有意义的社交、行动能力和安全前提下的最大自主。

points.en: The money worry has hard 2015 numbers: 16.3% of women 65 and over lived in low income versus 11.9% of men; among singles it was 33% of women and 29.8% of men, against just 8.7% of seniors living in couples. Late adults may literally weigh groceries against medication — and modern families shoulder less responsibility for elders than earlier generations did.
points.zh: 钱的焦虑有2015年的硬数据：65岁以上女性16.3%生活在低收入中，男性为11.9%；单身老人里女性33%、男性29.8%属低收入，而有伴侣的老人只有8.7%。老人可能真的要在『买菜还是买药』之间做选择——而现代家庭对老人承担的责任比上一代更少了。

atScene.en: Falling infants land headfirst: the head is a far bigger share of body weight than an adult's, and most infants cannot throw their arms out in time to break the fall — so any infant fall is a head, neck, and spine assessment until proven otherwise.
atScene.zh: 婴儿摔落多半头先着地：头占体重的比例远高于成人，而且大多数婴儿来不及伸手撑地——所以婴儿摔伤一律先按头颈脊柱损伤来评估，排除了才算数。

atScene.en: Count an infant's respirations by watching the abdomen rise, not the chest — the diaphragm does the breathing and the chest barely expands.
atScene.zh: 给婴儿数呼吸要看腹部的起伏而不是胸口——呼吸是膈肌在做功，胸廓几乎不扩张。

atScene.en: With very young patients, protect the routine: keep family close and familiar objects within reach — sameness is what keeps a toddler assessable.
atScene.zh: 面对年幼的患者，守住他的日常节奏：让家人在身边、熟悉的物件在手边——『一切如常』才能让幼儿配合你的评估。

atScene.en: Break the ice with a teddy bear: demonstrate each step on the bear before doing it to the child — toddlers and preschoolers follow show-and-tell far better than words alone.
atScene.zh: 用玩具熊破冰：每个操作先在熊身上演示一遍再做到孩子身上——对幼儿和学龄前儿童，『边演边讲』远比纯口头解释管用。

atScene.en: Adolescents interviewed in front of family may bend the truth to protect privacy or image — ask the sensitive questions in total privacy, where they can answer without constraint.
atScene.zh: 当着家人的面问诊，青少年为保住隐私和形象可能不说实话——敏感问题要挪到完全私密的场合问，让他能毫无顾忌地回答。

atScene.en: An older patient who hit their head and 'seems fine' is not cleared: brain atrophy means a subdural bleed can fill the empty space silently, and intracranial-pressure signs only appear once the void is full — keep suspicion high and reassess.
atScene.zh: 老人磕了头『看着没事』不等于真没事：脑萎缩留出的空腔能让硬膜下出血悄无声息地积聚，颅内压体征要等空腔灌满加压后才露头——保持高度怀疑，反复评估。

atScene.en: A murmur in an older heart or wheeze in an older chest is not automatically disease: stiffened valves can murmur without pathology, and weak airway walls can wheeze on strong inhalation — read these findings against the whole patient.
atScene.zh: 老人心脏有杂音、胸腔有喘鸣，不一定就是病：僵硬的瓣膜可以无病而杂音，无力的气道壁可以在用力吸气时塌陷发喘——这些发现要放回整个患者身上去解读。

confusions.en: Neonate versus infant: neonate is birth to 1 month; infant is 1 month to 1 year. Questions that say 'a 3-week-old infant' are testing whether you catch the mislabel.
confusions.zh: 新生儿与婴儿：新生儿是出生到1个月，婴儿是1个月到1岁。题干里写『出生3周的婴儿』，考的就是你能不能抓住这个错贴的标签。

confusions.en: Vital-sign directions with age run opposite ways: pulse and respirations FALL as children grow, while blood pressure RISES (it tracks body weight). Any option that has all three moving together is wrong.
confusions.zh: 生命体征随年龄的走向是相反的两条线：孩子越大，脉搏和呼吸越『降』，血压却越『升』（血压跟着体重走）。选项里三者同升同降的，直接排除。

confusions.en: Counting infant respirations at the chest: the diaphragm does the work and the chest barely moves — the abdomen is where you count. Watching for thoracic rise undercounts a struggling baby.
confusions.zh: 盯着胸口给婴儿数呼吸是个坑：呼吸靠膈肌，胸廓几乎不动——该数的是腹部起伏。只看胸廓起伏，会把一个呼吸费力的婴儿数『正常』。

confusions.en: Self-concept versus self-esteem: concept is how you perceive yourself; esteem is how you feel about yourself and fit with peers. Swap-the-definition is a free mark if you keep 'perceive' and 'feel' separated.
confusions.zh: 自我概念与自尊：概念是你怎么『认知』自己，自尊是你对自己的『感受』以及和同伴合不合群。把『认知』和『感受』分开记，这道换定义题就是送分。

confusions.en: Growth-spurt order: girls enter the adolescent spurt earlier, but boys finish taller and stronger. Options asserting 'boys develop earlier' or 'girls end up equal in strength' both contradict the text.
confusions.zh: 青春期猛长的顺序：女孩先进入猛长期，男孩却在结束时更高更壮。说『男孩发育更早』或『女孩最终力量相当』的选项都与原文相反。

confusions.en: First-week weight loss of 5% to 10% is normal fluid loss, not neglect or illness — the red flag is failing to regain from the second week, not the dip itself.
confusions.zh: 出生第一周掉5%～10%的体重是正常的体液丢失，不是被忽视也不是生病——真正的警示是第二周起不回升，而不是这个下坠本身。

confusions.en: The aging brain loses weight, neurons, and synapses — but its metabolic rate and oxygen consumption do NOT decline. The 'lower cerebral oxygen demand in the elderly' option is a trap.
confusions.zh: 老化的大脑丢重量、丢神经元、丢突触——但代谢率和耗氧量『不降』。『老年人脑耗氧需求降低』这种选项是陷阱。

confusions.en: Murmurs and wheezes in the old are not automatically pathology: stiff valves can murmur without disease, and weak airway walls can wheeze on strong inhalation. Age changes the baseline you are comparing against.
confusions.zh: 老人的杂音和喘鸣不自动等于疾病：僵硬的瓣膜可以无病而杂音，无力的气道壁可以在用力吸气时发喘。年龄改变的是你用来对照的基线本身。

mnemonics.name: 体重口诀 3.4-30-2-3
mnemonics.en: Birth 3.4 kg, gain 30 g a day, double by 6 months, triple by 1 year — the whole first-year weight story in four numbers.
mnemonics.zh: 出生3.4公斤，日长30克，6个月翻倍，1岁三倍——四个数字讲完第一年的体重故事。

mnemonics.name: 反射四连：惊·抓·寻·吸
mnemonics.en: Startle (Moro, arms fly open), Grasp (palmar, fingers close), Seek (rooting, head turns to the cheek touch), Suck (lips stroked). Four triggers, four responses, in the order a feed happens.
mnemonics.zh: 惊（Moro，双臂张开）、抓（掌握，五指合拢）、寻（觅食，碰脸颊就转头）、吸（碰嘴唇就吸吮）。四个触发、四个反应，正好是一次喂奶发生的顺序。

mnemonics.name: 推理三段 3P
mnemonics.en: Punishment (preconventional: avoid it, get what I want) → Peers (conventional: win approval) → Principle (postconventional: follow conscience).
mnemonics.zh: Punishment 罚（前习俗：躲惩罚、要好处）→ Peers 群（习俗：求认可）→ Principle 则（后习俗：凭良知）。三个P排出道德推理的升级路线。

mnemonics.name: 年龄段速查
mnemonics.en: 1 month–1 y infant · 1–2 toddler · 3–5 preschool · 6–12 school-age · 13–18 adolescent · 19–40 early · 41–60 middle · 61+ late adult.
mnemonics.zh: 1个月～1岁婴儿 · 1～2幼儿 · 3～5学龄前 · 6～12学龄 · 13～18青少年 · 19～40成早 · 41～60成中 · 61+成晚——一行背完所有分段题。

selfCheck.qEn: Recite the printed newborn baseline: pulse, respirations, systolic BP, oxygen saturation, and blood glucose floor.
selfCheck.qZh: 背出新生儿的印刷基线：脉搏、呼吸、收缩压、血氧饱和度、血糖下限。
selfCheck.aEn: Pulse about 140 beats/min; respirations 30 to 60; systolic BP 67 to 84 mm Hg; saturation 94% or greater; glucose at least 2.5 mmol/L at birth (3.3 from 1 month; the book prints 45/60 mg/dL).
selfCheck.aZh: 脉搏约140次/分；呼吸30～60次/分；收缩压67～84 mmHg；血氧≥94%；血糖出生时≥2.5 mmol/L（满1个月起≥3.3；书中印刷为 45/60 mg/dL）。

selfCheck.qEn: A parent asks if their baby's weight is on track. Give the first-year rules.
selfCheck.qZh: 家长问孩子体重长得对不对，说出第一年的规则。
selfCheck.aEn: About 3.4 kg at term birth; loses 5–10% in week one (fluid), regains from week two; then roughly 30 g/day — double birth weight by 6 months, triple by 1 year.
selfCheck.aZh: 足月出生约3.4 kg；第一周因体液丢5%～10%，第二周起回升；此后每天约30 g——6个月翻倍，1岁三倍。

selfCheck.qEn: You touch an infant's cheek and the head turns toward your finger. Name the reflex — and the one triggered by stroking the lips.
selfCheck.qZh: 碰一下婴儿的脸颊，他把头转向你的手指。这是什么反射？轻触嘴唇触发的又是哪个？
selfCheck.aEn: Rooting reflex; stroking the lips triggers the sucking reflex. (Moro = startle with arms flung wide; palmar grasp = fingers close on an object in the palm.)
selfCheck.aZh: 觅食反射；轻触嘴唇触发吸吮反射。（Moro＝受惊双臂张开；掌握反射＝手心放物五指合拢。）

selfCheck.qEn: Why can an older adult with head trauma look fine for hours or days, then deteriorate?
selfCheck.qZh: 为什么老人头部外伤后能『没事』好几个小时甚至几天，然后才恶化？
selfCheck.aEn: Brain shrinkage leaves a void inside the skull and stretches the bridging veins; trauma tears them and blood fills the void silently — intracranial pressure, and therefore the signs, only rise once the space is filled and pressurized.
selfCheck.aZh: 脑萎缩在颅内留出空腔并拉紧桥静脉；外伤撕裂桥静脉后，血悄悄灌进空腔——颅内压要等空腔填满加压才升高，体征也才随之出现。

selfCheck.qEn: Match the reasoning stage: acts to avoid punishment / seeks peer approval / follows conscience.
selfCheck.qZh: 配对推理阶段：为躲惩罚而行动／求同伴认可／凭良知行事。
selfCheck.aEn: Preconventional / conventional / postconventional — developed during the school-age years (6 to 12).
selfCheck.aZh: 前习俗／习俗／后习俗——都在学龄期（6～12岁）发展出来。

selfCheck.qEn: Adolescent vitals have settled into adult ranges. Quote them, and name the age band.
selfCheck.qZh: 青少年的生命体征已落入成人区间。报出数值和年龄段。
selfCheck.aEn: Ages 13 to 18: systolic BP 110–131 mm Hg, pulse 60–100 beats/min, respirations 12–20 breaths/min.

selfCheck.qEn: Two lung volumes move in opposite directions with old age — which, and with what consequence?
selfCheck.qZh: 老年时两个肺容积一升一降——是哪两个？后果是什么？
selfCheck.aEn: Vital capacity falls, residual volume rises: stagnant air lingers in the alveoli, gas exchange suffers, and hypercarbia with acidosis can develop even at rest.
selfCheck.aZh: 肺活量下降、残气量上升：陈腐气体滞留肺泡、气体交换受损，静息状态也可能发展出高碳酸血症和酸中毒。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Infant head-to-body proportion: from anatomy to BC's exam checklist
bcAlerts.topicZh: 婴儿头身比例：从解剖知识到 BC 考试清单
bcAlerts.bookEn: The chapter teaches the anatomy: an infant's head is a much larger share of body weight, infants land headfirst in falls, and the airway is short, narrow, and easily occluded.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 教材教的是解剖：婴儿头部占体重比例大、摔落时头先着地、气道短窄易堵。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's practical guidelines turn that anatomy into required actions: place a pad under an infant's shoulders to keep the airway neutral (the big occiput otherwise flexes the neck), palpate the brachial — not carotid — pulse, and limit suction to 5 seconds in an infant versus 10 in a child and 10–15 in an adult.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 实操指南把这条解剖变成了必做动作：给婴儿肩下垫垫布保持气道中立位（不垫的话大后脑勺会把颈屈起来）、摸肱动脉而不是颈动脉、婴儿吸引限时5秒（儿童10秒、成人10～15秒）。
bcAlerts.ref: EMALB BC Provincial Examination Guidelines p.45–46（Current to June 15, 2026）
